doc.title: David Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2022

title: Billy Harper clinic as generational translator; goodbyes
summary: Weiss describes helping students understand Billy Harper at a clinic as a generational translator, and the two say goodbye.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: They need, what do they call it, I just did a Billy Harper, we did a Billy Harper clinic like right before Covid, and it was like after a Cookers tour and I kept him out there to do a few other things, and I did some things for him. And I forgot, the director of the program, I told him yeah, I’m going to come along too. And he was like okay. What did I call it? A “generational translator.” I had to help the kids understand what Billy Harper was telling them.
In the context of what they knew.
I know exactly what you’re saying.

I was joking a little bit but it’s really true sometimes, it’s really true. It’s an interesting thing. These guys — never would these guys — they don’t really see what they’re saying, it’s not as clear as they hope or something like that. So they need somebody who can relate to an iPhone or something like that.
Right. Well thanks a lot for your time.
All right I’m going to sign off and then we’ll say our good-byes.
